Profile Management: Functional integration tests for self-service profile management (UserController / AuthController avatar)
A logged-in user retrieves their own profile and confirms the returned data matches their own account, not anyone else's.
column3:
1. Log in as any role and obtain a valid access token.
2. Prepare GET /api/v1/users/me with the Authorization header set.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response body to confirm it matches the caller's own account.
column4: 1. 200 OK; UserResponse for the caller's own account (id, email, fullName, phoneNumber, gender, roles[], status, etc).
column5: - Logged in with a valid access token.

Profile Management: Attempting to view the /me profile endpoint with no Authorization header at all is rejected before any account lookup happens.
column3:
1. Do not log in / discard any existing Authorization token.
2. Prepare GET /api/v1/users/me with no Authorization header.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response status and body message.

Profile Management: A logged-in user updates their own name, phone, gender, date of birth, and address in one request, and all fields are persisted.
column3:
1. Log in as any role and obtain a valid access token.
2. Prepare PUT /api/v1/users/me body {"fullName":"New Name","phoneNumber":"0912345678","gender":"MALE","dateOfBirth":"1998-05-05","address":"123 Main St"}.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response body to confirm every field was updated.
column4: 1. 200 OK; UserResponse reflects all updated fields.

Profile Management: Attempting to change one's own username to a value already taken by a different account is rejected, leaving the original username intact.
column3:
1. Log in and identify another account's existing username.
2. Prepare PUT /api/v1/users/me body {"username":"<another user's existing username>"}.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response and confirm the caller's username is unchanged.
column4: 1. 400 Bad Request, message "Error: Username is already in use!"; username unchanged.
column5: - Another account already has that username.

Profile Management: Changing one's own email to an address already registered by another account is rejected, while changing it to a genuinely unused address succeeds but resets the account's verification status.
column3:
1. Log in and identify another account's existing email.
2. Prepare and send PUT /api/v1/users/me body {"email":"<another existing user's email>"}; inspect the response.
3. As a currently-verified user, prepare and send PUT /api/v1/users/me body {"email":"brandnew@example.com"} (a genuinely unused address).
4. Inspect the response body and confirm the account's isVerified flag.
column4:
1. Step 1: 400 Bad Request, "Error: Email is already in use!"; email unchanged.
2. Step 2: 200 OK; email updated AND isVerified becomes false (must re-verify the new address before some flows work again).
column5: - Step 1 needs another account with a known email; step 2 needs an unused email.

Profile Management: Attempting to update the own-profile endpoint with no Authorization header at all is rejected before any changes are applied.
column3:
1. Discard any existing Authorization token.
2. Prepare PUT /api/v1/users/me with no Authorization header and any body.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response status and body.

Profile Management: Changing password with the correct current password and a genuinely different new password succeeds immediately, and every previously issued refresh token is invalidated, forcing re-login on other devices.
column3:
1. Log in and obtain both an access token and a refresh token for a known-password account.
2. Prepare and send PUT /api/v1/users/change-password body {"currentPassword":"<correct>","newPassword":"newPass123"}; inspect the response.
3. Attempt POST /api/auth/refresh-token using the refresh token issued in step 1.
4. Inspect the refresh attempt's response.
column4:
1. Step 1: 200 OK, body {"message": "Password changed successfully!"}.
2. Step 2: refresh fails (401) — all of the user's refresh tokens were deleted as a side effect of the password change.

Profile Management: Changing password while supplying an incorrect current password is rejected, and the account's real password remains unchanged.
column3:
1. Log in as any role with a known current password.
2. Prepare PUT /api/v1/users/change-password body {"currentPassword":"wrong-password","newPassword":"newPass123"}.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response and confirm the password was not changed (e.g. by logging in again with the old password).
column4: 1. 400 Bad Request, body {"error": "Incorrect current password."}; password unchanged.

Profile Management: Attempting to change password to the exact same value as the current password is rejected, preventing a no-op password change.
column3:
1. Log in as any role with a known current password.
2. Prepare PUT /api/v1/users/change-password body {"currentPassword":"<correct>","newPassword":"<same value>"}.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response status and message.
column4: 1. 400 Bad Request, body {"error": "New password must be different from the current password."}.

Profile Management: Attempting to change password with no Authorization header at all is rejected, and this endpoint's error body is a raw JSON string rather than the {"message":...} shape used elsewhere.
column3:
1. Discard any existing Authorization token.
2. Prepare PUT /api/v1/users/change-password with no Authorization header and any body.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response status and body shape.
column4: 1. 401 Unauthorized, body {"error": "Unauthorized"} — note this endpoint's error responses are raw JSON strings, not the {"message":...} shape used elsewhere.

Profile Management: Uploading a small, valid JPEG under the 2MB limit succeeds for every eligible role, and the returned avatarUrl points at the newly uploaded image.
column3:
1. Log in as an eligible role (LEARNER, TRAINER, TRAINER_LEAD, or ADMINISTRATOR) and prepare a 500KB .jpg image file.
2. Prepare POST /api/auth/profile/avatar as multipart form-data with key "file" set to that image.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response body's avatarUrl and confirm the image is reachable.
column4: 1. 200 OK; UserResponse with avatarUrl pointing to the newly uploaded Cloudinary image.
column5: - Logged in as an eligible role; a small valid image file available.

Profile Management: Uploading an avatar image larger than the 2MB limit is rejected, and the account's existing avatarUrl is left untouched.
column3:
1. Log in and prepare an image file confirmed to exceed 2MB.
2. Prepare POST /api/auth/profile/avatar as multipart form-data with that oversized file.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response and confirm avatarUrl is unchanged.
column4: 1. 400 Bad Request, body "Error: Avatar file must not exceed 2MB."; avatarUrl unchanged.
column5: - Logged in; an oversized image file available.

Profile Management: Uploading a disallowed file type such as .gif or .pdf as an avatar is rejected by content-type validation, and the existing avatarUrl is left untouched.
column3:
1. Log in and prepare a .gif or .pdf file.
2. Prepare POST /api/auth/profile/avatar as multipart form-data with that file.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response and confirm avatarUrl is unchanged.
column4: 1. 400 Bad Request, body "Error: Avatar must be a .jpg, .jpeg, or .png image."; avatarUrl unchanged.
column5: - Logged in; a non-jpg/png file available.

Profile Management: Submitting the avatar upload request with no file part attached at all is rejected by validation before any upload is attempted.
column3:
1. Log in as any eligible role.
2. Prepare POST /api/auth/profile/avatar with an empty/missing file part.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the response status and message.
column4: 1. 400 Bad Request, body "Error: Avatar file is required."
